$comment: Antigravity CLI on a Google AI Pro/Ultra subscription.
STOP. Read `cache.kind` before using anything in this file.
Google prices context caching as STORAGE OVER TIME - a per-token-hour charge for keeping a
cache alive - not as a write multiplier against a TTL the way Anthropic does. The two are not
the same arithmetic wearing different numbers, and no conversion between them was found that
could be defended. Under a subscription the user-visible currency is neither: it is quota, and
no public figure maps Antigravity's quota onto cached tokens.
So `cache.kind` is `unpriced`, which is a real state the code understands: CostModel.canPriceCache()
returns false, and the cache clock refuses to spend on keepalive or compaction for this provider
rather than acting on an invented number. A worker on this model still runs work, still gets
preempted at a window boundary, and still hands off - it simply will not pay to hold a cache
open, because nobody here knows what that costs.
This file becomes useful the moment somebody measures it. Until then its honesty is its value:
an invented multiplier would be indistinguishable from a measured one at the point of use.

MODELS: `agy models` in a Windows PTY, agy 1.5.7, 2026-11-12: gemini-4-hydrogen (low|medium|high|xhigh), gemini-4-argon, gemini-3.8-flash, claude-opus-5-5 and claude-sonnet-5-5 each list low|medium|high; gpt-oss-120b lists medium only. Claude 4.6 is retired alongside the previously retired Gemini models, retained for history. New models have unknown context windows and token prices; no figures are copied from another provider.
Effort is separated into `effort_levels` and passed via `--effort` (low|medium|high) rather than
being blended into model identifiers. Antigravity serves Claude and GPT-OSS models alongside Gemini
— so 'this task needs Claude' does NOT imply 'this task needs a claude-code worker', and
capability routing has to be asked about the model, not the vendor.

$plans_comment: ⚠️ TWO POOLS, ONE SUBSCRIPTION, AND THE SPLIT BETWEEN THEM IS A HEURISTIC.
Antigravity meters Gemini apart from Claude/GPT but bills one $20. `pool_shares` says how the
one subscription is charged across the two, and the numbers are the operator's judgement call,
not a published figure: Claude/GPT draws its window far faster than Gemini does, so most of the
money is attributed to the Gemini pool. The shares sum to 1, which is what keeps a week that
fills BOTH pools reporting one week's subscription rather than two.
⚠️ REVISED 2026-09-06, from 80:20 to 90:10. The first split made a Claude/GPT task on this
provider read as several times the price of a Gemini one on Analytics > Statistics > Model
Price per Task - $4 of the $20 attributed to a pool that serves a small minority of the runs
here. Still a judgement call and still not a measurement: what would settle it is a published
per-pool cost, and until one exists this number is the operator's belief with its date on it.
`claude` and `gpt` both name the same window (the panel heading slugifies to `claude-and-gpt`)
and so carry the same share; a window is only ever counted once, at the largest share that

quota.$comment: Two separately metered pools on one account - Gemini apart from Claude/GPT - measured 2026-08-27 by reading the `/usage` panel, which renders both groups' windows. This block previously said kind 'unknown', probe 'none', windows [], which contradicted both the adapter's quotaProbe: 'cli' and a parser that had been reading four windows for two days. The ids here are what parseUsageScreen emits; the exact group slug follows the panel's heading wording, so `pool` is matched by containment rather than by equality.

$owed: Cache pricing: is it storage-per-token-hour on a subscription at all, or is caching simply not billed to a subscriber? Until this is known, cache.kind stays `unpriced`.
Context windows are the published figures for each family, not read from the CLI - `agy models` reports ids and display names only.

Whether a quota window exists at all, and over what period: /usage measured 2026-08-27. Antigravity /credits was measured 2026-09-04 in a real PTY on agy 1.1.26 (Google AI Pro tier): the panel renders `Remaining AI Credits: AI Credits not enabled (enable in /settings)` without dollar balance, credit count, expiration, or tier. Even with useAiCredits: true in settings, no credit balance or spend meter is published for individual consumer/Pro accounts. spendProbe remains `none` and no speculative parser is committed.
Nothing here is metered: agy writes conversations as SQLite, so the transcript tailer reads nothing. See capabilities.meteredFromTranscript.
